instruction.default: Choose the first burn and the number of phasing orbits, then execute. The lab burns back at the same point.
instruction.description: Instruction shown at the top of the control panel

requirements.title: Requirements

gap.title: Distance to the client (km)
gap.description: Distance to the client in km (positive: the client is ahead; negative: it is behind)

budget.title: Propellant (m/s)
budget.description: Propellant for both burns, in m/s

requirements.description: The requirements to meet, in order (one to six), each a distance to the client, the most phasing orbits allowed and the propellant for both burns. When you change them, change the text version of the block too.

tolerance.description: Distance to the client, in km, at which the rendezvous counts as met

showPrediction.description: Show the path and the predicted final gap before executing (for novices: it removes the need to calculate)

exaggeration.description: How many times the distance between the two craft is magnified in the 3D view (the plot is at true scale)

secondsPerOrbit.description: Duration of one simulated orbit on screen, in seconds

servicerColor.description: Colour of your servicer and of its path

allMet.description: Title of the mission card once all are met

freeFlight.description: Eyebrow of the mission card once all are met

catchUp.description: Title of a requirement where the client is ahead

letCatch.description: Title of a requirement where the client is behind

briefAhead.text: The client is {gap} km ahead. Meet it within {orbits, plural, one {# orbit} other {# orbits}}, with at most {budget} m/s of propellant for both burns.
briefAhead.description: Text of the mission card; gap and budget are formatted numbers

briefBehind.text: The client is {gap} km behind you. Let it catch up within {orbits, plural, one {# orbit} other {# orbits}}, with at most {budget} m/s of propellant for both burns.

freeBrief.text: Try any manoeuvre: nothing is scored any more.
freeBrief.description: Text of the mission card once all are met

burnNone.description: Value of the burn slider at zero

retrograde.description: Left end of the burn slider (keep the arrow)

prograde.description: Right end of the burn slider (keep the arrow)

bothBurns.description: Small text under the propellant meter

client.description: Meter label: where the client is

gapAlongside.description: Where the client is: next to you

ready.text: Set the first burn and the number of phasing orbits, then execute.

reduced.text: Animation off (reduced motion): each manoeuvre shows its result at once.

burn1Retrograde.text: Burn 1, retrograde: the far side of your orbit drops.
burn1Retrograde.description: Status line during the first burn

burn1Prograde.text: Burn 1, prograde: the far side of your orbit rises.
burn1Prograde.description: Status line during the first burn

burn1None.text: No burn: you stay on the circular orbit.
burn1None.description: Status line when the burn is zero

burn2.text: Burn 2 at the same point: back on the circular orbit.
burn2.description: Status line during the second burn

met.text: Requirement {i} met: the client is {where} at the end.
met.description: Result; where is a gapAhead, gapBehind or gapAlongside text

final.text: At the end the client is {where}.
final.description: Result of a missed requirement, followed by the reason

whyNoBurn.text: Without a burn both craft keep the same period, so the gap does not change.

whyPrograde.text: You burned prograde: you climbed, each lap took longer and the gap grew.

whyRetrograde.text: You burned retrograde: you dropped, each lap took less time and you moved further ahead.

tooLittle.text: Not enough drift: burn more, or fly more orbits.
tooLittle.description: Reason of a miss, followed by the rule

tooMuch.text: Too much drift: you overshot. Burn less, or fly fewer orbits.
tooMuch.description: Reason of a miss, followed by the rule

rule.text: At 500 km, each m/s gains about 17 km per orbit.
rule.description: Rule of thumb recalled after a miss

overBudget.text: You met the client, but the two burns cost {cost} m/s and the budget is {budget} m/s. Spread a smaller burn over more orbits.

tooLong.text: You met the client, but this requirement allows at most {orbits, plural, one {# phasing orbit} other {# phasing orbits}}.

allDone.text: Every requirement is met. The lab stays open: try any manoeuvre.

predicted.text: Predicted: the client {where} at the end.
predicted.description: Prediction help (where is a gap text)

view.description: Accessible name of the view button, before the view name

clientTag.description: Tag of the client satellite in 3D

scale.text: In 3D, the distance between the craft is magnified {k} times.

dv.description: First burn selected, in m/s (negative: retrograde)

step.description: Index of the current requirement (the number of requirements once all are met)

events.name: manoeuvre
events.description: A manoeuvre has been flown for an open requirement.

events.name: requirement_met
events.description: A requirement is met; the next one opens.

a11y.description: Three-quarter view of the Earth from space, with day and night sides, clouds and a thin atmosphere. A circular orbit 500 km up carries your servicer (orange) and the client satellite (violet). When you execute a manoeuvre, the servicer fires at the burn point, flies the phasing orbits below or above the circle, then fires again at the same point; a plot shows its true position relative to the client, along the orbit and in altitude.
a11y.keyboard: Tab reaches the controls: the burn slider (arrow keys, 0.5 m/s steps), the orbits group (arrow keys) and Execute. Shortcuts: R adds 0.5 m/s retrograde, P adds 0.5 m/s prograde, 1 to 3 set the orbits, X executes, Space pauses.
a11y.dragAlternative: Dragging the view turns the camera around the Earth; the View button switches between the same angles without dragging.
